narrative.title: The Sensor That Pinged One Time Too Many
narrative.scenario: A sensor network logs ID pings in an audit trail where every sensor reports an even number of times except one faulty unit that reports an odd number. Rebuilding a tally table is overkill for the gateway firmware; instead it folds every ping ID through one accumulator, in which paired pings annihilate and the lone repeat-offender survives.
narrative.inputFormat: An array arr of n positive integers where exactly one value occurs an odd number of times.
narrative.outputFormat: The value with the odd occurrence count.

testCases.explanation: Pairs of 1s and 2s cancel; three 3s fold down to a lone survivor.
One pair cancels and the third ping stands alone.

hintLevels: Level 1: Think cancellation, not counting — pairs erase themselves.
Level 2: x ^ x = 0 and XOR commutes, so the fold of the whole array keeps only the odd-occurring value.
Level 3: No hash map needed: the accumulator is order-independent and uses a single integer of memory.
